title: The Horizon of Station Meridian Again
premise: Tamsin Winterbourne, the last investigator of Station Meridian's impossible accidents, has spent nine years secretly maintaining a beacon that broadcasts a false armistice signal—the only thing keeping two hostile fleets from annihilating the colony between them. When the colony's children begin sharing one dream of a 'second sun,' Tamsin realizes the beacon is failing and the truth it suppresses is leaking into minds. As she races to repair the lie, she falls for Idris Vale, a fleet auditor sent to find exactly what she's hiding. In the end, Tamsin must choose: let the fleets collide and save her own soul, or sacrifice her anonymity—and Idris's trust—by broadcasting the whole truth, ending the war but exposing herself to justice outside any law.
about_author: Jude Sandoval is a former maritime insurance adjuster who traded claims files for star charts after a decade of investigating disasters nobody wanted explained. They write from a converted lighthouse on the Atlantic coast, where they remain stubbornly convinced that every lie worth telling deserves a good maintenance schedule.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Tamsin performs her nightly maintenance on the hidden beacon in Meridian's derelict upper spire, cataloguing its decay with an investigator's precision. Her POV establishes her ritualized invisibility and the guilt she carries like ballast. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking dread.

chapters.title: Impossible Accident No. 44
chapters.summary: A cargo lift falls through three sealed decks with no mechanical cause; Tamsin investigates officially while privately suspecting the beacon's field fluctuations. Her POV reveals her dual life—bureaucrat by day, saboteur of truth by night. Beat: the first crack in her control.

chapters.title: Children of the Second Sun
chapters.summary: Colony teacher Amara Osei reports that eleven children drew identical pictures overnight: a second sun over the station. Tamsin interviews them, recognizing the image as the beacon's fail-state iconography. Beat: cold recognition that the secret is dreaming its way out.

chapters.title: The Auditor Arrives
chapters.summary: Idris Vale steps off the quarterly transport with fleet credentials and a mandate to audit Meridian's 'anomalous energy expenditures.' Tamsin, assigned as liaison, lies smoothly for the first time in years. Beat: attraction sharpened by mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: Ledgers of Light
chapters.summary: Idris traces power draws toward the spire while Tamsin falsifies consumption records in real time. Alternating POVs show two careful minds circling each other. Beat: the investigation becomes a courtship neither will name.

chapters.title: What the Dream Wants
chapters.summary: The shared dream spreads to forty children, then a dockworker. Tamsin descends into the beacon's core and finds the memory lattice degrading, leaking its payload. Beat: horror reframed as responsibility—she built this cage of silence.

chapters.title: Nine Years Ago
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young investigator Tamsin discovers the beacon after the accident that killed her mentor, and chooses concealment over disclosure, believing peace outweighs truth. Beat: the origin of her self-imposed sentence.

chapters.title: Coffee at Odd Hours
chapters.summary: Idris and Tamsin share a 3 a.m. break in the mess hall; he admits he doesn't believe his own employers' story about Meridian. Vulnerability exchanged under fluorescent light. Beat: love begins where duty frays.

chapters.title: The Fleet That Waits
chapters.summary: POV shift to Admiral Serevan aboard the Concordance flagship, holding position beyond sensor range, awaiting a signal that has begun to stutter. Beat: the distant threat acquires a patient, terrible face.

chapters.title: Accident No. 45
chapters.summary: A second impossible event—a vacuum breach that heals itself—confirms the beacon's field is warping local physics. Tamsin realizes repairs require parts from the quarantined lower foundry. Beat: the clock becomes audible.

chapters.title: Amara's Question
chapters.summary: Teacher Amara confronts Tamsin: the children aren't frightened of the dream, they're comforted by it, and Amara wants to know why Tamsin isn't. Beat: an ally gained who demands honesty as the price.

chapters.title: Audit Findings, Draft One
chapters.summary: Idris compiles his report and deliberately omits the spire anomaly, testing his own integrity. His POV exposes his disillusionment with fleet justice. Beat: he chooses Tamsin over the fleet without admitting it.

chapters.title: The Foundry Descent
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Idris raid the flooded lower foundry for lattice components, nearly drowning when the field fluctuates again. Forced intimacy in the dark. Beat: trust forged in rising water.

chapters.title: What Idris Knows
chapters.summary: Idris reveals he was sent because both fleets suspect Meridian harbors 'the Armistice Engine'—and his real orders are to destroy it if found. Beat: the man she loves is her executioner on standby.

chapters.title: Repair Night
chapters.summary: Tamsin rebuilds the memory lattice alone while the children's dream intensifies colony-wide; adults now wake weeping. She buys the colony another month and ages a year. Beat: triumph shadowed by futility.

chapters.title: Serevan's Patience Ends
chapters.summary: Admiral Serevan detects the lattice surge and moves the Concordance fleet one jump closer, dispatching a probe ship. Beat: consequences approach at lightspeed.

chapters.title: The Probe
chapters.summary: The fleet probe docks under diplomatic pretense; its captain, Halvorsen, is Idris's former commander and sees through him instantly. Beat: Idris's double life collapses inward.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Liar
chapters.summary: Halvorsen privately offers Idris clemency for naming the saboteur. Idris stalls, buying Tamsin days he may not be able to keep buying. Beat: love against duty, made literal.

chapters.title: Dream Logic
chapters.summary: POV of eight-year-old Juno Park, who explains the dream simply: the second sun is 'the truth waiting to hatch.' Children begin gathering at the spire base. Beat: innocence as prophecy.

chapters.title: The Colony Remembers
chapters.summary: Adults start recalling fragments of the pre-beacon war—faces, ships, the accident Tamsin covered. Public order frays; the council demands answers she cannot give. Beat: the lie decays faster than she can patch it.

chapters.title: Council of Ash
chapters.summary: Tamsin testifies before the colony council, committing perjury with perfect calm while Amara watches, knowing. Beat: justice outside the law begins here—institutional law failing openly.

chapters.title: Idris Finds the Spire
chapters.summary: Following the children, Idris reaches the beacon chamber and finds Tamsin inside it. The confrontation neither wanted: gun drawn, truth finally spoken. Beat: the midpoint detonation.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Tamsin shows Idris the full archive—the war crimes both fleets committed, which the beacon's false armistice buried along with the evidence. Beat: understanding without forgiveness.

chapters.title: Halvorsen's Deadline
chapters.summary: Halvorsen gives Idris twelve hours or takes the station by force. Meanwhile Serevan's counterpart, Warlord Kesh of the Rimward fleet, also detects the beacon. Beat: pincers closing from both sides.

chapters.title: Kesh Descends
chapters.summary: Rimward scouts infiltrate Meridian's docking ring; skirmish in the cargo bays kills three colonists. Tamsin's cover story dies publicly. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Choice Framed
chapters.summary: Tamsin lays out the options: restore the lie (temporary), stay silent (annihilation), or broadcast everything (war-crimes tribunals, her own prosecution, possibly civil war). Idris refuses to choose for her. Beat: agency reclaimed.

chapters.title: Amara Organizes
chapters.summary: Amara marshals the teachers and older children to shelter colonists and document everything—building the record that honest reckoning will need. Beat: hope as infrastructure.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Halvorsen's strike team breaches the spire; Idris turns his weapon on his own commander to protect the beacon long enough for Tamsin to finish final calibrations. Beat: betrayal transformed into loyalty.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Begins
chapters.summary: Tamsin reprograms the beacon from suppression to revelation, streaming the archived truth to both fleets and every screen on Meridian. Beat: terrifying liberation.

chapters.title: Fury of the Concordance
chapters.summary: Serevan, exposed, orders bombardment rather than face tribunal; his own officers hesitate as the evidence reaches their private channels. Beat: tyranny cracking from within.

chapters.title: Kesh's Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Warlord Kesh proposes joint occupation of Meridian as a neutral truth-and-reconciliation site—an offer with obvious traps. Tamsin negotiates via open channel, unarmed. Beat: diplomacy as the last impossible accident.

chapters.title: Mutiny in the Dark
chapters.summary: Concordance crew members, confronted with archived footage of their own dead, refuse fire orders; Serevan is confined by his bridge. Beat: justice arriving sideways, through conscience.

chapters.title: The Second Sun Rises
chapters.summary: The beacon completes its broadcast; the children's dream ends, replaced by ordinary dreams. On the surface, colonists watch both fleets hold position—not peace, but a ceasefire of shame. Beat: exhausted awe.

chapters.title: Arrest Warrant, Unsigned
chapters.summary: The provisional council debates Tamsin's fate: nine years of stolen consent versus nine years of saved lives. She requests no counsel. Beat: accountability embraced, not fled.

chapters.title: Idris's Report
chapters.summary: Idris submits his true findings, implicating himself, Halvorsen, and the fleet command that ordered the original cover-up. Beat: duty redefined as truth-telling.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Tamsin testifies to everything—the mentor's death, the choice, the maintenance, the cost. Amara and Juno speak for the colony. Verdict deferred to a truth commission both fleets must join. Beat: catharsis through testimony.

chapters.title: Sentences
chapters.summary: Halvorsen is remanded; Serevan awaits fleet trial; Tamsin receives supervised restitution—rebuilding the beacon as an open, honest archive anyone can read. Beat: justice outside the law becoming law worth trusting.

chapters.title: Maintenance Schedule, Revised
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Idris work the spire together, converting the beacon into Meridian's public memory. Quiet domesticity inside unfinished history. Beat: love surviving its trial.

chapters.title: What the Children Dream Now
chapters.summary: Juno and the children paint a new picture: one sun, and below it a small figure keeping a light lit. Tamsin finally lets herself be seen. Beat: grace.

chapters.title: The Horizon of Station Meridian
chapters.summary: One year later: the truth commission convenes on-station, both fleets' delegations arriving under the beacon's honest light. Tamsin, no longer invisible, watches the horizon not for threats but for arrivals. Final beat: the future, unhidden.
